texts.preamble: Page No.# 1/6 vs Mridul Deka And Anr on 1 August, 2023
texts.facts: However, considering the fact that the petitioner even after obtaining stay order from this Court on 14.08.2015 failed to join his duty for about 16 months and approached the respondent authority with a joining report only on 02.01.2017, therefore the petitioner will not be entitled to any backwages for the intervening period w.e.f. 14.08.2015 to 02.01.2017. However, considering the fact that his termination is found to be bad in law while the petitioner admittedly is again out of service since 16.03.2017, ends of justice would be seemed if he is given 50% of backwages w.e.f 17.03.2017. 16. It is also noticed that the contract appointment of the petitioner is only for 3 years w.e.f. 01.01.2015 and therefore, the same is due to come to an end on 31.12.2017. No doubt, further retention of the petitioner will be at the discretion of the respondent authority but however, such discretion should be exercised on sound principles governing employment and with an open mind." The respondent No. 1 herein was employed as a Data Entry Operator by the appellant herein on contractual basis vide communication dated 21.09.2012, for a period up to 31.07.2012. He joined service on 01.10.2012. The appointment of the respondent No. 1/writ petitioner was governed by the Memorandum of Understanding signed between the employee and the Employers, i.e. Food Safety & Page No.# 3/6 Standards Authority of India (FSSAI). The appointment was on periodic basis and to be renewed from time to time. Such renewal was made for a period of three years w.e.f. 01.01.2015 vide Office Order dated 31.12.2014 which inter alia provided that the continuance of the contractual appointment would be subject to evaluation of performance and conduct of the employee on annual basis. An Office Memorandum dated 23.04.2015 was issued to the respondent No. 1/writ petitioner seeking his explanation regarding an act of misconduct, wherein the respondent No. 1/writ petitioner was alleged to be heard hurling an insinuation that Page No.# 1/6 vs Mridul Deka And Anr on 1 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106367536/ 2 the Deputy Director, FSSAI, was indulged in harassment of Assamese people in Nagpur. The respondent No. 1/writ petitioner furnished his explanation to the said Office Memorandum on 27.04.2015. However, the explanation, not being found satisfactory, was rejected and the contractual service of the respondent No. 1/writ petitioner was terminated vide order dated 22.06.2015. Being aggrieved, the respondent No. 1/writ petitioner filed the writ petition No. WP(C) 4686/2015 challenging the order dated 22.06.2015. The writ petition was taken up for hearing on 14.08.2015 and, while issuing notice thereof to the respondents, the effect and operation of the order of termination was stayed. However, notwithstanding the said order dated 14.08.2015, respondent No. 1 / writ petitioner continued to remain absent from duty for about a period of one year and six months and returned to resume duty only on 02.01.2017. Subsequently, on an Interlocutory Application being filed by the appellants herein seeking modification of the order dated 14.08.2015, the Court observed that the respondents (i.e. appellants herein) were at liberty not to act upon the joining report of the employee dated 02.01.2017. This direction was given on 27.02.2017, which was challenged by the writ petitioner/respondent No. 1 herein in an appeal before the Division Bench of this Court.
texts.arguments: The appellant/employer has now approached this Court through this intra-court writ appeal for assailing the direction given by the learned Single Bench to the extent they were directed to pay 50% of the backwages w.e.f. 17.03.2017 to the employee/ respondent No. 1 herein. 3. Learned counsel Mr. M. K. Das, representing the appellants vehemently and fervently urged that the learned Single Bench was not justified in interfering with the order of termination because the respondent No. 1/writ petitioner being a contractual employee had misbehaved with the superior officer by hurling racist insinuations. He thus urged that the impugned order is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. His alternative submission was that if this Court is not inclined to interfere in the impugned order to the extent the order of termination was [LEAKAGE_MASK], the fact remains that the respondent No. 1/writ petitioner was admittedly out of service from 16.03.2017. He pointed out that after the order dated 27.02.2017 modifying the interim order dated 14.08.2015 had been passed, the respondent No. 1/writ petitioner was again removed from service and he never worked on the post thereafter and, thus, the direction to pay him 50% backwages for the period, during which he did not work, cannot be said to be justified by any stretch of imagination. 4. Learned counsel Mr. T. Deori, representing the respondent No. 1/writ petitioner vehemently and fervently opposed the submissions advanced by the appellants' counsel. However, Mr. Deori was not in a position to dispute the factual aspect that the respondent/writ petitioner never worked on his contractual post from 17.03.2017 onwards.
